A bottle stands upright on the tabletop beyond the bottom of the ramp, with a book standing upright a short distance farther along the same path. The bottle and book are separated, and nothing touches anything else at t=0.
rows.what_happens: Gravity takes over and the sphere rolls down the inclined_plane onto the tabletop. It hits the bottle, and the bottle tips away from the impact. The falling bottle then strikes the book, and the book begins to tip as well. The sphere continues onward after the first collision while the two upright objects react one after the other, showing a brief chain of motion and balance loss.
rows.counterfactual: Change only one physics-related aspect: move the bottle slightly farther from the bottom of the ramp. Everything else stays the same. The sphere then rolls out onto the tabletop without hitting the bottle, so the bottle and book remain still.

rows.title: Book nudged into a bottle
rows.initial_state: A book rests flat on the table near a bottle that stands upright a short distance away. A sphere is placed on the table behind the book, aligned so it can travel forward and strike the book. At t=0 the sphere is already moving toward the book, while the book and bottle are at rest.
rows.what_happens: The moving sphere hits the book and sends the book sliding toward the bottle. The book then hits the bottle, and the bottle tips and begins to rock and settle under gravity. The book slows after the impact and comes to rest while the bottle finishes its motion nearby.
rows.counterfactual: The only change is that the bottle starts farther away from the book. The sphere still hits the book, but the book no longer reaches the bottle, so the bottle stays upright and only the book moves.

rows.title: Ball strikes bottle into a second bottle
rows.initial_state: On the floor, a ball is already moving in a straight line toward two bottles. The first bottle stands upright ahead of it, and the second bottle stands upright a short distance beyond the first, both aligned with the ball’s path and separated from each other.
rows.what_happens: The ball hits the first bottle head-on and pushes it forward. The first bottle then moves into the second bottle, and the second bottle is struck and starts to topple away from the impact. The ball continues forward after the first impact while the bottles separate and fall or slide depending on the contact forces.
rows.counterfactual: The only change is that the second bottle is moved farther away from the first bottle at t=0. The ball still hits the first bottle, but the first bottle no longer reaches the second one, so the second collision does not happen.

rows.title: Book steadies a bottle on a ramp
rows.initial_state: A book rests on the upper part of an inclined_plane that stands on the floor. A bottle sits upright on the sloped surface partway down the ramp, with a sphere placed behind it farther up the same path. All bodies start apart except for resting contact with the ramp, and the sphere is already moving when the clip opens, rolling downhill toward the bottle.
rows.what_happens: The sphere rolls down the incline and hits the bottle. The bottle starts to move downslope, then the book blocks its path and it rocks into contact with the book. The bottle and book settle into a temporary balance where the bottle is supported between the ramp and the book, with only small adjustments as the motions die out.
rows.counterfactual: Change only one initial detail: move the book a little farther uphill on the incline. With everything else unchanged, the rolling sphere still hits the bottle, but the bottle no longer reaches the book, so it continues farther down the ramp instead of settling into balance against it.

rows.title: Book balanced on a wedge edge
rows.initial_state: A book stands on the floor with one long edge resting on the sharp top edge of an inclined_plane, and a cube sits on the floor beside the base of the ramp, clear of the book’s path. At t=0 the book is already supported in a precarious balance by the ramp edge, with no other contact. The cube is at rest.
rows.what_happens: Gravity keeps the book pressed against the ramp edge as it makes a small, visible rocking motion. The book shifts slightly, then settles into a new balance point without falling off the support. Nothing strikes the cube, which remains still throughout.
rows.counterfactual: If the book were placed flat on the floor instead of resting on the edge of the inclined_plane, it would stay motionless and would not rock into a new balance point.

rows.title: Swaying bottle on a hanging rope
rows.initial_state: A hanging_rope stands fixed to the floor-mounted support area and a bottle is tied to its free end, hanging at rest in the air. A ball sits on the table several widths away from the hanging bottle, aligned so that it will travel toward the bottle when released. At t=0 the ball is already moving, heading toward the hanging bottle while the bottle is momentarily still.
rows.what_happens: The moving ball strikes the hanging bottle and transfers momentum to it. The bottle swings away from the impact, briefly moving through a dynamic balance between gravity and the rope’s tension as it arcs. As the bottle swings back, the ball continues away and slows from the earlier collision, leaving the rope-and-bottle system in a visibly oscillating state before the motion begins to settle.
rows.counterfactual: Change only one physics-related aspect: the ball starts at rest instead of already moving. Everything else remains the same, so the bottle is not struck and stays hanging still.

rows.title: Ball rolls down ramp into a bottle and topples a mug
rows.initial_state: A basketball rests near the upper end of an inclined_plane that stands on the table, with the ramp sloping down toward the floor-side end. A bottle stands upright on the flat surface directly in the basketball’s path at the bottom of the ramp. A mug stands upright a short distance beyond the bottle, farther along the same path. All three objects are separated at t=0.
rows.what_happens: The basketball is released and rolls down the inclined_plane under gravity. It leaves the ramp and continues along the flat surface, hitting the bottle. The bottle is pushed forward and tips as it moves, then strikes the mug. The mug is knocked over and tumbles away while the basketball continues a short distance and slows from surface friction.
rows.counterfactual: Change only one initial aspect: the bottle is placed slightly farther to the side, out of the basketball’s path. The basketball still rolls down the ramp, but it misses the bottle, so the mug is never hit and remains standing.

rows.title: Ball rolls through a balanced bottle
rows.initial_state: On the floor, a bottle stands balanced upright in the sphere’s path. A book rests flat a short distance beyond the bottle, and a box is placed farther along the same straight line. At the start of the clip, the sphere is already rolling along the floor toward the bottle. The book and box are motionless and separated so the rolling sphere can strike the bottle first and then set off the later contacts.
rows.what_happens: The rolling sphere hits the bottle and knocks it off balance. The bottle tips and falls into the book, pushing the book forward. The book then slides into the box and nudges it over, creating a brief chain of motion that settles as the objects spread out and come to rest.
rows.counterfactual: The same setup, except the sphere starts at rest instead of already rolling. Without the incoming motion, the bottle is never struck, so the bottle, book, and box remain still.

rows.title: Ball strikes a bottle into a second object
rows.initial_state: A ball is already moving along the table at t=0. Ahead of it on the same path, a bottle stands upright on the table. Farther along that path, a box stands still on the table with space between it and the bottle. The floor and walls are present in the environment.
rows.what_happens: The moving ball hits the bottle head-on and drives the bottle forward. The bottle then travels into the box and strikes it. After the second impact, the box shifts away while the bottle and ball continue to move and slow down from friction on the table.
rows.counterfactual: Change only one physics-related aspect: place the bottle slightly off the ball’s straight path at t=0. The ball then passes by without striking it, so the bottle never reaches the box.

rows.title: Bottle topples after a rolling sphere hits it
rows.initial_state: A bottle stands upright on the floor near one side of the scene. A sphere rests farther away on the same floor, aligned so it can roll straight toward the bottle. A book stands on the floor beside the bottle, clear of the sphere’s path and not touching anything. At t=0 the sphere is already moving toward the bottle, while the bottle and book are at rest.
rows.what_happens: The moving sphere rolls across the floor and hits the bottle squarely. The bottle is knocked off balance and begins to tip over. It rotates as its center of mass shifts past its base, then falls onto the floor. The sphere continues forward a short distance after the collision and slows down.
rows.counterfactual: Change exactly one physics-related aspect: the sphere starts at rest instead of already moving. Everything else remains the same. With no incoming motion, the bottle is never hit and stays upright.

rows.title: Wobbling mug on the edge of a book
rows.initial_state: A book lies flat on the table. A mug sits near one edge of the book, placed so that it is balanced and slightly overhanging the edge, but still at rest at t=0. A sphere rests on the table to the side of the book, on the tabletop and not touching the book or the mug.
rows.what_happens: As the clip opens, the mug is already near the brink of motion because it is placed past its balance point on the book. It begins to tip and rock under gravity, with its weight shifting past the support area. The mug teeters, then either settles back briefly or tips farther as the imbalance grows, demonstrating a changing balance rather than a steady rest. The sphere stays motionless on the table throughout.
rows.counterfactual: If the mug were placed a little farther inward on the book at t=0, it would remain balanced and still instead of beginning to tip.

rows.title: Ball hits a tilted book and topples a bottle
rows.initial_state: On the table, a book is standing partly open and tipped so one cover forms a slanted surface. A bottle stands upright near the higher side of the book, with the ball held above the table and in line with the slanted book surface. Nothing is touching at t=0, and the ball is already moving toward the book as the clip opens.
rows.what_happens: The moving ball strikes the slanted book surface and bounces off with a changed direction. The impact nudges the book, which shifts and then tips further under gravity. As the book tilts, it knocks into the bottle. The bottle loses support, wobbles, and then topples over onto the table.
rows.counterfactual: The same setup, except the ball starts at rest instead of already moving. With no incoming impact, the book is not struck, so the bottle stays upright.

rows.title: Sphere rolls down ramp into a book and topples it
rows.initial_state: A book stands upright on the floor, away from the ramp. A sphere rests near the upper end of an inclined_plane that stands on the floor, with the ramp leading down toward the book’s position. The sphere is released at t=0 and is otherwise unsupported.
rows.what_happens: Gravity pulls the sphere down the inclined_plane. The sphere rolls along the ramp, reaches the floor at the bottom, and continues forward. It hits the book, and the impact pushes the book out of balance. The book tips over and falls flat on the floor.
rows.counterfactual: The only change is that the book is laid flat on the floor instead of standing upright. The sphere still rolls down the inclined_plane and hits it, but the book does not topple.
